title: League Start Like A Pro In 0.5

segments.text: Does it feel like every league start you excitedly load up your favorite creator's build guide,
follow it through to maps, only to realize you can't afford the headhunter, rings and
mirrored tier bow they somehow already have on day 2?
To make matters worse, the items you want are increasing in value with each day that
passes and regardless of how long you farm, you just can't seem to increase anything other
than your deaths?
Today that changes.
I'm Viking0071, the guy in charge of gearing over half of the top 10 players in the last
3 PoE2 leagues.
In this video, I'll give you a 3 step plan to finding items, creating items and storing
your earnings in things that actually keep up with inflation.
Step 1.
What to farm.
Most people will attempt to rush T15 maps in order to unlock the best items, however
I think they're missing something huge.
Let me explain.
In Path of Exile 2, map tier determines monster level.
This monster level is displayed on the map device before opening a map or in the top
right corner of your screen once you are in a map.
Each tier of map you go up increases this monster level by 1, starting at monster level
65 for tier 1 maps and increasing to monster level 79 in tier 15 maps.
This monster level determines the level of items which it will drop.
If we kill a monster in a tier 1 map, we get a level 65 base.
There are some exceptions to this rule, but that's not important for now.
The key idea here is simply that certain very powerful mods unlock at low tiers.
Let's take a look at boots as an example.
The most important stat on boots is movement speed and defenses.
Here we have 2 pairs of boots.
Both have the same amount of movement speed and very similar defense stats.
The crazy part?
The boots on the left were found in tier 1 maps, whereas the boots on the right were
found in tier 15 maps.
Here's another wild example.
On bolts, the only thing people care about is life and resistances.
While at tier 7 maps, we get access to the same life and resistance mods that we would
in tier 15.
If we know when these powerful mods unlock, then we know what to search for in every tier
of map and more importantly, which tier of maps actually justify their difficulty increase.
To save you the 7000 hours it's taken me to learn these, here are the most important map
tiers.
Tier 1, level 65.
These will be called Ancient Waystones next league.
Tier 7, level 71.
This will be called Refined Waystone 2.
And finally, tier 11, level 75.
These will be called Pristine Waystone 1.
In tier 1 maps, you are hunting for boots because you get movement speed.
You're hunting for helmets for access to plus 2 minion and crit chance and gloves for access
to plus 2 melee, crit chance and attack speed.
In tier 7 maps, you'll gain access to up to 40% resistances.
So here we want to hunt items that require resistances.
The best example of these is bolts, armors and resistance rings.
Armors also gain the added benefit of extra defense stats at this tier.
In tier 11, we gain access to most maximum flat damage rolls.
So here we want to search for rings for the flat damages, gloves again for the flat damages
and then amulets because at this tier amulets gain the ability to roll plus 3 to all spell,
plus 3 to minion, plus 3 to projectile and plus 3 to melee skills.
Martial weapons are also pretty good in tier 11 because we can roll near maximum damage
on them.
What does this actually mean?
Well this means that if your build can comfortably farm tier 1 maps but struggles to farm tier
7 maps, then it's best to just stick in tier 1 maps until you are strong enough to go up
to tier 7.
Likewise, if your build is strong enough to farm tier 10 maps but not tier 11 maps, then
you would be better off just farming tier 7 maps.
Now that you know what to farm, let's move on to step 2.
I'll show you how to quickly and cheaply craft the bases you found in step 1.
Step 2.
Early League Crafting.
Most people overcomplicate this step.
You do not need mirror tier knowledge, 40 browser tabs or a spreadsheet made by a Harvard
graduate.
You just need to know 3 core crafting systems that are completely broken during league start.
These are blue currencies, essences and the most overpowered strategy, putrefactions.
Once you understand these 3 systems, you can take cheap tier 1, 7 and 11 bases and consistently
turn them into items which increase your power or sell for some sweet profits.
Blue currencies.
These are transmutations, augmentations and regal orbs.
Transmutations turn a normal item into a magic item and add one modifier.
Augmentations add an additional modifier to a magic item and regals turn a magic item
into a rare item adding a modifier.
You want to spam transmutations and augmentations on every item you pick up.
Regals you only want to use on items with 2 good stats.
If you aren't familiar with what stats are good on items, here's an easy formula.
Firstly, look for item exclusive modifiers.
These are the modifiers that I just pointed out to you in step 1.
Things like movement speed on boots and plus 2 skills on amulets.
Secondly, look for any resistance modifiers.
A minimum of 30% is acceptable.
And thirdly, you look for defense modifiers.
Strength bases want armor, dexterity bases want evasion and intelligence bases want energy
shield.
Now don't make this complicated.
Big number equals good, small number equals bad.
Essence crafting.
There are over 60 essences in Path of Exile 2.
For league start, we really only care about 6 of them.
The first two are for weapons.
This is your perfect essence of sorcery, which is used to add plus 2 skills to 1s and staffs
and I would only use these on bases that have high spell damage.
And then the perfect essence of battle, which adds plus to all attack skills on martial
weapons.
Again, I would only use these on bases that already have high damage.
Personally, I don't do much crafting with these two essences.
I use them specifically for gearing up my character.
The next 4 essences are resistance essences, namely thawing for cold, insulation for fire,
electricity for lightning and ruin for chaos.
These will add the corresponding resistance modifier to your item.
I would suggest only using these on belts that have at least a life modifier and 1 resistance
above 30% or on boots that already have 30% movement speed and another resistance modifier.
Now for the most overpowered early league crafting method, the omen of putrefaction.
When you activate an omen of putrefaction in your infantry, your next desecration will
add 6 unrevealed modifiers.
For armors we use a preserved rib, for weapons we use a preserved jawbone and for jewelry
we use a preserved collarbone.
This is completely overpowered for 2 reasons.
Firstly, we don't need to use any exalts on the item like we would have to if we used
the blue currencies or essences.
And secondly, we get 3 choices on every modifier, which essentially means we're going to see
a total of 18 modifiers and then be able to select our favorite ones to create an item
that's usable.
This massively increases our chances.
Let's head down to the wall of souls and I'll show you how this actually works.
Here we have a pair of boots with bad modifiers.
We activate our omen of putrefaction and use a preserved rib on them.
This gives us our 6 modifiers.
Now we go over to the lurking creature and of course rub him for a little bit of luck.
Once you are feeling sufficiently lucky, open up the wall of souls and begin unveiling
your modifiers.
Here we'll use the same rules that I gave you earlier.
Firstly we are looking for our key modifier, movement speed.
After that we check for resistances and finally we check for defensive rolls.
Then we select the one with the highest number, in this case 122 armor.
On the next page we immediately see our 30% movement speed, following our rules we click
on that immediately.
On the next page we see defensive modifiers and of course following our rules we select
the one with the highest number.
Now we are looking for resistances.
We get fire on the first page and lightning on the next roll.
Our final mod, we don't get offered any resistances or any defensive stats, but we have strength
and this is a strength base, which means that's a good modifier, so we'll take that.
Now we have a completed pair of boots, which is absolutely insane for a pair of boots that
you can find in tier 1.
Also don't forget to add sockets and quality, because you won't be able to do this after
using your omen of putrefaction.
The best items to use the omen of putrefaction on in order are boots, rings, armors, gloves
and finally quivers.
I wouldn't suggest using them on weapons or belts, because in my testing we've had really
really really bad results on those two items.
If you're still struggling to understand or you want more information on when powerful
mods unlock, I've included links in the description for both my Twitch and the Mirror Tier Discord.
Feel free to pop in and ask any questions.
Ok, now you know where to find items and how to craft them.
Let's move on to step 3, where I'll show you how to invest your currency to make sure that
you keep up with inflation.
Step 3.
Beating Inflation.
Every league I see the same thing happen.
People farm all day and stack up all their currency in divines, trying to get to their
first mirror.
On day 1 they manage to farm 20 divines and they check the price of mirror.
Ah, great, mirror's only 100 divines.
Five more days and I'll be able to buy my mirror.
Five days later, when they go to buy their mirror, it's now 10,000 divines.
What went wrong?
Well firstly, you need to understand that everything in Path of Exile 2 is priced in
regards to mirrors, because mirrors is the highest form of currency.
If the div price goes from 5 exalts to 10 exalts, it's because of mirrors.
If ritual omens are too expensive, it's because of mirrors.
And if Fabgoon gloves go from 1 divine to 10 divine, it's because of mirrors.
So how do we actually beat this?
Well it all comes down to where you invest your divines at the end of the day.
The goal is to invest your divines in things that are going to move up with the price of
mirror, until you've saved enough that you can actually outright buy your mirror.
Now I don't expect you to become a pro Ange flipper or to know what Fabgoon is going to
play before he does.
Instead, I'll give you this no brain formula that you can use in every single league.
Firstly, you want to get Omen of Abyssal Echoes.
Secondly, Omen of Whittling or Omen of Light.
Thirdly, Hinnikorah's Lot.
And finally, your mirror.
Let's go into a bit more detail.
The goal is to start at the bottom and move your investments up as you get more currency.
Omen of Abyssal Echoes is really the entry level here.
This is for the boys that are struggling.
A couple of exalts, maybe one or two divines.
You want to invest in Omen of Abyssal Echoes because they get used more and more as the
league goes on.
Not only for putrefactions, but also every time an Omen of Light is used, people use
an Abyssal Echoes to get more value from their light.
The next thing you want to invest in and really where the bulk of your investment should be
throughout the league is in Omen of Light and Omen of Whittling.
There's two really key reasons for this.
The first reason is that these Omens are used on every mid to high level craft and
multiple of them are used for each of these crafts.
And the second reason is because crafters and groups will hoard these Omens in order
to protect their crafts.
Let me explain that.
Groups and mirror crafters will create mirror items.
And those mirror items will get copied by other players and those players will pay a
fee for copying it.
Now if Omen of Whittling and Omen of Light are very cheap, well then nobody's going to
make mirror copies.
They'll simply craft the items themselves.
So big crafters and big groups buy out all the stock of Omen of Whittling and Omen of
Light to ensure that their prices stay high.
Because high prices means more mirror services.
The worst case scenario, if the price of these Omens drop, they're still protected
because they can simply then use the Omens to craft gear which then sells for a premium.
So really there's no way for you to lose or for groups to lose on these two investments.
You should just follow in their footsteps.
Buy as many as you possibly can.
Personally I prefer to be heavy on Whittlings as opposed to Lights but really that's just
personal preference and it's up to you.
Now once you've started to acquire a lot of these Omens, if you're sitting on 100, 200,
300 of these Omens and you want to start investing into something else, you've got a bit of extra
savings, what you're going to want to do is put your money into Hinnikorah's Locks.
These are relatively cheap at the beginning of it because there's little to no use for
them.
But as we get later into the league and people have really, really good expensive items that
they want to corrupt or sanctify, well then the Hinnikorah's Locks start to get used a
lot more and their price drastically goes up.
So you should be trying to get as many Whittlings and Lights as possible and then putting a
certain portion of that into Hinnikorah's Lock, generally funds that you're not going
to need.
This is like a long term savings.
And boys, it's pretty simple.
Just repeat that process.
Get as many Omen of Whittlings and Omen of Lights as you can, put some of it into Hinnikorah's
Locks and your money will grow with the price of Mirror.
Once you've acquired enough of those resources, simply sell them on the market and acquire
your first Mirror.

and let me know in the comments if you'd like more videos like this throughout the entirety
